Node's `path.isAbsolute` throws `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]` on a non-string. A config with `jira.credentialSource = { type: 'file' }` and no `path` (or a numeric `path`) therefore makes `validateConfig` throw instead of returning the aggregated error list: `validateJiraConfig` has already pushed `jira.credentialSource.path must be absolute`, but `validateConfig` does not short-circuit, so the throw escapes. In `kstack-jira.mjs` `loadJiraState`, `validateConfig` is called outside the try/catch, so the TypeError surfaces as a generic failure with `EXIT.STATE_ERROR` (2) rather than the intended `EXIT.CONFIG_INVALID` (1); in `kstack-config.mjs main()` it is an uncaught throw. This is pre-existing (unchanged since round 4), reachable only from a locally malformed config, and has no confidentiality or integrity impact — the credential boundary is untouched — so it does not block this round, but the round-6 fix makes the asymmetry visible and it should be closed as a follow-up.","unresolvedQuestions":["Lexical-vs-realpath divergence for `draft`: `validateCredentialFilePathContainment` compares raw `repoRoot` to raw `source.path`, while `validateCredentialFileConfig` compares `fs.realpathSync` of both. A repo root or credential path containing a symlinked directory component can therefore be accepted by `draft` and rejected by every other command, or (in the reverse direction, e.g. `<repo>/link-to-outside/cred.json`) rejected by `draft` while accepted at credential-use time. Is the resulting split — offline `draft` usable/unusable inconsistently with online commands on such configs — accepted as the intended cost of a syscall-free check?","`options.command` is a caller-supplied trust input to `validateConfig`. A programmatic caller can do `loadJiraState({ command: 'draft' })` and then `runJiraCommand(state, 'submit', ...)`, obtaining the relaxed static validation for a credential-consuming command. The CLI never does this, and `resolveCredentials`/`validateCredentialFileHandle` re-enforce containment on a live descriptor, so this is defence-in-depth only. SEC-R5-1 is correctly closed as Opus prescribed in round 5, and I verified each element of the claim independently from the packet.\\n\\n1. Syscall-free lexical check for `draft`: `validateCredentialFilePathContainment` uses only `path.relative`, `path.isAbsolute`, and `path.sep` — all pure. There is no `fs` reference in its body, so the offline `draft` path performs no filesystem access on the credential path. The containment predicate is byte-identical in structure to the one inside `validateCredentialFileConfig` and to `repoContains` in `kstack-jira.mjs` (`relative === ''` OR not `..`-prefixed and not absolute ⇒ inside ⇒ error), so the three implementations agree on the lexical semantics.\\n\\n2. Existence-requiring checks still skipped for `draft`: symlink (`lstatSync`), regular-file, dev/ino stability, uid ownership, and mode-bit checks all live in `validateCredentialFileConfig` and are unreachable from the `draft` branch. The behaviour is pinned by two tests — `offline draft does not require an available or valid credential file` (missing/unreadable/malformed credential, all outside the repo, all succeed) and `offline draft rejects a lexically inside-repository credential path without accessing it`, which asserts both the containment message and `doesNotMatch(/ENOENT/)`, i.e. it demonstrates positively that no stat/realpath was attempted on a non-existent path.\\n\\n3. Every other command unchanged from rounds 4/5: the dispatch is a single `if (options.command === 'draft') … else validateCredentialFileConfig(…)`. `validateCredentialFileConfig` is untouched (still stat-level, still no content read), `kstack-config.mjs main()` calls `validateConfig` with no `command`, so the CLI `validate`/`show` paths take the full check, and the runtime enforcement in `resolveCredentials` → `validateCredentialFileHandle` (descriptor-bound realpath, `O_NOFOLLOW`, dev/ino re-check, `repoContains`) is unmodified. `repoRoot` derivation (`dirname(dirname(resolve(configPath)))`) matches `loadJiraState`'s.\\n\\n4. Strict-mode guard is behaviour-preserving: `typeof actionError === 'object'` is true for every `Error` instance, so all real throws still receive `releaseError` exactly as before; the guard only suppresses the assignment for thrown primitives, which would otherwise be a strict-mode TypeError masking the primary error. The `withDraftLock preserves an action error and exposes a concurrent release-fencing error` test still asserts the `JiraQueueError` + `releaseError` shape and passes.\\n\\n5. No regression evidence: 68/68 tests in `tests/jira-queue.test.mjs` pass with no skips, 9/9 files pass across the suite, and the lock/fence, duplicate-evidence, verification-interval, redaction, and doctor assertions are all still green.\\n\\nThe error string pushed by the new function is a fixed literal with no interpolation, so the relaxed path cannot disclose the configured credential path in output — marginally better than the full check, which sanitizes but still surfaces `error.message`.\\n\\nFollow-ups, neither gating: (a) add the `typeof source.path === 'string'` guard to `validateCredentialFileConfig` so a malformed `{ type: 'file' }` config returns exit 1 with the aggregated errors instead of throwing a TypeError; (b) consider asserting in `runJiraCommand` that the executed command matches the command the config was validated for, so the `draft` relaxation cannot be carried into a credential-consuming call by a programmatic caller. Both are small, independent, and safe to land after this No regression evidence: 68/68 tests in `tests/jira-queue.test.mjs` pass with no skips, 9/9 files pass across the suite, and the lock/fence, duplicate-evidence, verification-interval, redaction, and doctor assertions are all still green.\\\\n\\\\nThe error string pushed by the new function is a fixed literal with no interpolation, so the relaxed path cannot disclose the configured credential path in output — marginally better than the full check, which sanitizes but still surfaces `error.message`.\\\\n\\\\nFollow-ups, neither gating: (a) add the `typeof source.path === 'string'` guard to `validateCredentialFileConfig` so a malformed `{ type: 'file' }` config returns exit 1 with the aggregated errors instead of throwing a TypeError; (b) consider asserting in `runJiraCommand` that the executed command matches the command the config was validated for, so the `draft` relaxation cannot be carried into a credential-consuming call by a programmatic caller.
